$comment: Mod catalogue. One entry per swappable mod asset, keyed by generation where the two cars differ. See mx5-mod-modelling-brief.md §8 for the schema and §7.1 for how `slot`/`optionId` map onto the controls carData.json already defines. `scripts/validate-mod.mjs` reads this file and checks each exported .glb against its entry.
$slots: `slot` is a CarConfig field name and `optionId` an id already present in carData.json's aeroParts/wheelStyles for that slot. A mod with slot:null has no control yet and cannot ship — see brief §7.1.
$anchors: `anchors` names base-asset nodes the mod must reach. blender/anchors.json holds their measured boxes; the validator asserts the exported mod comes within `anchorToleranceMm` of each, which is the machine-checkable form of 'nothing floats'.
$attribution: `derivedFromBaseMesh: true` means the geometry was derived from a CC-BY car asset and ATTRIBUTION.md must record the modification. See brief §4.
$roadmap: What we intend to build, in build order. `mods` is what actually exists; `node scripts/mod-status.mjs` joins the two and says what to pick up next. Everything here is ND-only for now because the NA is not imported into the working .blend.
$origin: `originMm` is the app-space point a mod's geometry is exported relative to. Body mods omit it and ship in absolute app coordinates. Wheels set it to their contact patch, because the app parents them to a pivot already sitting there — see brief §2.2. The validator offsets the bbox by it before checking anchors.

mods.uiHint: 12,376 tris — kept at full resolution, no decimation was needed
mods.$sourced: Derived from a THIRD-PARTY sourced asset, not built by this pipeline. Models/meister_l1_3p/scene.gltf, "Meister L1 3P" by Wilbruh (sketchfab.com/mirz1911), CC-BY-4.0. See ATTRIBUTION.md.
mods.$note: First test of importing a real wheel model rather than building one from primitives. Rim only (paired with our own tyre/disc/caliper). Both source textures carried real trademarks — a WORK Wheels(R) logo decal and a MEISTER wordmark baked into the cap texture — the decal mesh was deleted outright and the cap retextured flat, per brief §2 (no trademarked names, badges or logos). Scaled from its own measured outer radius (227.9mm raw) to match RIM_R. Materials were renamed into the MOD_* contract rather than recreated from scratch, but this makes less difference at runtime than it sounds: CarModel.setWheelFinish() unconditionally overwrites colour, metalness, roughness and clearcoat on the whole 'rim' class on every config apply, the same as it does for every other wheel — verified live, selecting 'Chrome' repaints it to #eef2f4 like any other wheel. What actually carries over untouched is the mesh geometry and topology — the real point of this comparison — not the material values.
mods.$decision: 12,376 tris was already comfortably within the normal 18,000 wheel budget on import, so the decimated comparison pass was dropped rather than kept — decided after visual comparison in-app.
mods.$bugs: Building this found and fixed three real pipeline bugs, all now in mx5_lib.py: (1) a radius measured from bounding-box CORNERS combines the y-extreme and z-extreme as if the same point, measuring the box's diagonal rather than the true circular radius — scaled the wheel ~30% too small on the first attempt; (2) the imported mesh's parent chain (Sketchfab_model -> fbx -> RootNode -> Circle -> mesh) was left intact, and once the scratch import collection was deleted those parent Empties became collection-orphaned — the glTF exporter then silently dropped every mesh with an unresolvable parent from a use_selection export, no error, just six missing primitives; (3) clean()'s remove_doubles does not touch truly loose vertices, which a Decimate modifier routinely strands at UV seams — the decimated pass shipped 732 of them before clean() gained an explicit loose-vertex pass.

mods.uiHint: 267,926 tris — 15x the normal wheel budget. Comparison only; expect a real performance hit, especially at 4 wheels.
mods.$sourced: Derived from a THIRD-PARTY sourced asset. Models/rays_gramlights_57dr/scene.gltf, "RAYS GramLights 57DR" by ilvskf (sketchfab.com/ilvskf), CC-BY-4.0. See ATTRIBUTION.md.
mods.$note: Second sourced-wheel test, and a genuinely different problem from WS01: 338,167 raw triangles (a hard-surface CAD-style export, no textures at all — every material is a flat PBR factor, so any branding has to be geometry, not an image), and its rotational axis is raw Blender Y, not X like Meister. Confirmed numerically rather than visually: Blender's viewport stopped compositing partway through this session (stale frames regardless of camera state), so orientation rests on mesh position analysis — both branding meshes and the shallow barrel shells sit in the same narrow negative-Y band, while a deep structural mesh extends to positive Y, putting the outward face at -Y. A +90-degree rotation about Z before the usual translate-and-scale corrects it. Two branded meshes (a black sticker and a yellow/gold badge, both off-axis at one clock position) are deleted outright, same rule as WS01.
mods.$budget: triangleBudget is set to reflect reality (270000), not the normal 18000 wheel figure — validate-mod.mjs would otherwise fail this honestly, which is correct behaviour for every OTHER wheel; this one is deliberately over budget for a side-by-side look, not a shipping recommendation.
mods.$bugs: The sticker-removal step matched by exact original name and silently removed nothing on the first attempt — the glTF importer auto-suffixes on every re-run (Object_11.001 -> Object_11.002), so an exact match works once and then matches nothing forever after. Fixed by matching on the base name with the suffix stripped, and by turning the failure into a hard error (RuntimeError if the removed count doesn't match the expected count) rather than a silent no-op — the same bug in a different guise very nearly shipped both trademarks a second time.

mods.$sourced: Derived from a THIRD-PARTY sourced asset. Models/wheels/scene.gltf, "Wheels" by Wasi204 (sketchfab.com/hafizzwaseem88), CC-BY-4.0. See ATTRIBUTION.md.
mods.$note: Wheel_01 of 30 in the pack. Unlike WS01/WS02 (bare rims, needing our own tyre/disc/caliper/lugs built from primitives) this source is a complete self-contained assembly per wheel — a rim, a tyre and an already-modelled disc+caliper — so this mod ships none of mx5_lib's revolve()/radial_copies() geometry at all, only what the source authored. Each Wheel_NN in the pack sits on a display-tray placement (an arbitrary showcase rotation, not the wheel's real shape); orientation was recovered by measuring in that node's own local frame rather than raw import-world space, which resolves to a clean thin-axle/matched-diameter disc. Scaled uniformly so the tyre's own outer radius lands on TYRE_R (320.5mm), the same anchor every other wheel mod's tyre is built to, rather than RIM_R, since the source's tyre is real geometry here, not something built around a bare rim afterward.
mods.$materials: Deliberately NOT renamed into the MOD_* contract (materialContractExempt: true) — the source ships a small per-wheel baked texture (AO/highlight detail) that is very likely why it reads as a real wheel at under 1,000 triangles, and MOD_Rim's flat colour would replace that texture outright. wheel_01_metal/wheel_01_rubber keep their own name and texture and are mapped to a new 'static_textured' surfaceClasses.json entry that nothing tints — the Wheel finish picker has no effect on this mod, by design, confirmed with the user before building.
mods.$pilot: First of a 3-wheel pilot batch (WP01-WP03) proving a single parametrized Blender function (blender/mods/WP_wheelpack.py, build_wp(n, mod_id)) against the 30-wheel pack, rather than one bespoke script per wheel like WS01/WS02 needed. Later extended to 13 (WP04-WP13) once the pipeline held up.
mods.$bugs: Two rounds of the same bug. Round 1: WP01-WP03 shipped backwards (the back of the disc, the hub-mount side, not the finished face a spoke gap should reveal) — only surfaced from user feedback on the actual screenshots, since a numeric bbox/radius match can't tell front from back. Fixed with a blanket 180-degree flip applied to every wheel. Round 2: building WP04-WP13 immediately tripped a hard assertion showing Wheel_06, Wheel_07 and Wheel_13 measuring rim-and-brakes on the OPPOSITE local-frame side from every other wheel checked so far, which read as a second authoring convention worth respecting — so build_wp() was changed to flip only the wheels whose own measurement called for it, and shipped that way. It was WRONG: user inspection in the running app found 6, 7 and 13 backwards too. The measured asymmetry was noise, not a real second convention — a per-wheel heuristic that looks reasonable is not the same as one that is correct, and this one was guessing right 10 times out of 13. build_wp() now applies the same 180-degree flip to every wheel unconditionally, with no per-wheel branching at all.

mods.$note: 12-spoke cross-mesh, matching carData's bbs_mesh spokeCount rather than the brief's nominal 8 for this design. One wedge — a radial spoke plus a diagonal brace to the next spoke's root — circular-arrayed 12x, per the brief's own instruction never to model individual struts. The brace is what makes it read as lattice rather than spokes with lines on them.

Not in the brief's catalogue, which only specifies aftermarket designs. oem_16_silver has been a real carData.json wheelStyle id since before this pipeline existed, and like every unmapped aero id before it, selecting it did nothing — it silently showed the same 17in Design wheel. Thin flat spokes, a 25mm lip (the catalogue's own lipDepth figure), near-flush dish: deliberately the plainest wheel in the set. Fixes one more line of README's 'Wheel style is inert' limitation. The default wheel (oem_17_design) is deliberately left unmapped so the stock render keeps using the real authored OEM wheel rather than an approximation.

The sill's own body-paint skin, extended down 60mm and out 25mm from its lower edge with a t^2 ramp that is zero at the OEM line, the same seamless-join technique as the boot spoilers. Both ends terminate flush into the arches because the donor panel's own shape ends there — nothing is trimmed.

Same geometry as RA06, carbon finish. Both option ids already existed in carData.json's sideSkirts list (oem_extensions and carbon_extenders); this is a second mod id in the family rather than a schema change, the same pattern W01/W07/W04 use across wheelStyle.

New panel, not derived — the rear valance has no diffuser insert to lift. Mount height is a ray-cast of the valance underside (270..300mm across x -300..300, not the brief's nominal figure), kicking up 12deg to the trailing edge. Four strakes at x 0/+-280/+-560. A 40mm cut-out at x -354..-220 clears the measured exhaust tip position.
Same geometry as RA04, carbon finish, matching track_diffuser already in carData.json.

The true donor is the OEM lower-lip TRIM piece (BumperF 6.001_109), not the wider painted fascia — its bbox min y is 169, matching FA03's independently-measured 'bumper's lowest point'. The painted panel above it stops higher because there is an intake cutout there; the black lip fills below it. Extended 55mm down and 25mm forward with an 8-degree flare, ramped to zero at y230 so the join is seamless.
mods.$conflict: Marked incompatible with FA03 — both occupy the frontLip slot's geometry at the same bumper station.

mods.$note: Four 76mm tips 2x2 at x +/-95 / +/-195 offset from the measured OEM centreline (x -287, not the vehicle centreline), in a gloss-black surround valance. MOD_Titanium is a static purple-blue tint, not the gradient the brief describes — no bake step in this pipeline yet.

A domed disc conformed to the quarter panel at the same measured mount point as DT01, 4mm proud. Needs the Phase 3 schema extension before it can ship; marked incompatible with DT01 since both replace the same OEM mast.

Sits where the OEM mast MEASURES — app x -581, on the vehicle's RIGHT. The brief's nominal position had it on the left. The mount height and the panel normal are both ray-cast; the quarter is 47 degrees off vertical there, so the axis is pulled most of the way back to upright and the gasket takes up the rest, which is what a real antenna base wedge does. 20 degrees of rearward rake on top.
mods.$partial: Grooves are turned rings rather than a true helix — invisible at this size, and a real helix costs a swept curve for nothing.

mods.$note: A ribbon — two rows of vertices 45mm apart following a hand-placed hanging curve, solidified 3mm — rather than a swept tube. A tube squashed flat still catches light like a cylinder, and webbing does not. Sits at x -480, clear of the exhaust at -287. Needs a CarConfig field before it can ship.

Each canard's inboard end is placed off a ray-cast of the bumper's flank, not off its bounding box. The bumper is 857 wide at its widest and about 600 at z 1790, so the first attempt put all four canards in mid-air with daylight behind them. They now bury 25mm into a skin measured at 683 and 694. Needs a CarConfig field before it can ship.
mods.$partial: No 25-degree rearward sweep — block() rotates about the lateral axis only.

mods.$note: The eye is an annulus revolved about the lateral axis rather than a block with a boolean hole — a spun ring has the hole by construction and cannot fail the way a boolean can. Protrudes to z 2041 against a nose at 1958, with its mounting boss buried at 1813. MOD_AccentPaint because these are always anodised. Needs a CarConfig field before it can ship.

The boot lid's own rear 260mm, lifted 85mm on a t^2 ramp. Zero slope where it meets the panel, so the front row of vertices is still exactly the boot lid — the brief calls a visible step at the front edge the single most common failure here, and this makes it impossible rather than careful.
mods.$budget: Over the brief's 3000. A panel-derived part inherits the donor's density; the alternative is modelling it freehand, which forfeits the guaranteed shut line. 163 kB, so the cost is bookkeeping rather than performance.

mods.$note: The mild option in the same slot as the ducktail and the wing: 140mm of strip, 35mm rise, with the ends flicking up a little more than the centre so it does not read as a shelf laid across the boot.
mods.$budget: Over the brief's 1500, for the same reason as RA01.

mods.$note: Two hoops 140mm apart with crown spacers and a full-width harness bar at y 950. Both hoops sit inside z -950..-1090, the band where the cabin tub actually offers a surface — outside it the mesh has gaps and a probe returns nothing, which would put footplates at an assumed height.
Built from the same script as EX06 so the pair stay consistent — the brief's warning here is that misaligned twin tips are instantly visible, and two scripts drift.

The oval mouth is a squashed revolve, so the bore stays a real tube rather than a flat plate with a dark decal. Needed a new `twin_oval` id in carData.json — the exhaust catalogue had four and three were taken, and the remaining one is titanium, which this is not.
mods.$partial: Offered on the ND only, because that is the only generation with the asset.

mods.$note: 38mm OD tube, every end on a 100x100x6 footplate at a probed deck height — 797 under the hoop legs, 753 under the stays. Station chosen by probing: at z -820 the cabin mesh is thin over the soft-top well and reports a deck of 853 from one ray height and nothing from any other, so the hoop would have stood on the well cover.
mods.$clash: Occupies the same space as the soft top when the roof is UP — the ND stows its top behind the seats, so this is a roof-down part. Not marked incompatible because the app has no way to express 'requires roof down' yet.

mods.$note: Every plate height is ray-cast from the bonnet at that exact station, so the plates lie on the curved panel rather than hovering at a nominal height — this is a part whose whole job is to look bolted down. Needs the Phase 3 schema extension: CarConfig has no bonnet-hardware field.
mods.$partial: The lanyard is a straight bar; the brief asks for a cable with natural sag.

mods.$note: Sits where the OEM tips MEASURE — app x -354..-220, off-centre to the vehicle's right — not on the centreline the catalogue drawing implies. The tip is a real tube with a separate dark bore sleeve; a solid rod with a dark cap reads as a toy.

Flat and level at app y 150, just under the bumper's measured lowest point of 168, projecting to a leading edge at z 2055 against a nose at 1958. Following the bumper's curve downward instead would make it a valance, which is a different part. Rods run from inside the plate up to y 470, well inside the bumper's 175..644 band, so both ends are buried rather than touching.
mods.$partial: Rods are square-section and vertical; the brief specifies 10mm round and raked back.

mods.$note: Base plates start at app y 858, which is the boot lid's height measured by ray-cast at the upright stations rather than the brief's nominal figure — that assumes a different datum and would leave the uprights hanging. 1400 span against a 1790 cap (body width minus 150). The element is an inverted cambered aerofoil at 8 degrees, trailing edge high.
mods.$partial: No bolt heads on the base plates and no adjuster hardware at the upright/element joint. 320 triangles against a 6000 budget — there is plenty of room to add them.

mods.$note: ET0 puts the mounting face on the centreline, so 114mm of barrel sits outboard of the spoke face — that is the design. The lip is a separate object on MOD_Alloy while the face is MOD_Rim, so the wheel-finish picker recolours the face and leaves the lip polished. 24 exposed bolts, without which a lip this deep does not read as three-piece.
mods.$deviation: The brief lists this as NA-only, but carData.json already offers watanabe_rs on the ND and the NA is not imported into the working .blend, so it is built at 17x9 ET0 for the generation that can show it.

mods.$note: ET25 and genuinely concave spokes — the face is pulled 34mm inboard at the hub and rises to the lip plane at the rim, following (1-t)^1.6. That curve is the design's whole character; flat slabs at constant depth are a different wheel.
mods.$partial: No machined dimple detail near the hub, and the spoke section is a chamfered slab rather than a rounded trapezoid.

mods.$note: Origin is the contact patch, so the app's existing wheel pivot gives it diameter, camber and track for free. Modelled for the LEFT side; place the right-hand instance with rotation.y = PI, which is rigid and so does not flip winding. Outer diameter is 641mm because that is what the ND's wheels measure — building to the 205/45R17 spec instead would shift ride height on every car fitted with it. Ships a caliper, which makes CarConfig.caliperColor live for the first time.
mods.$partial: Spokes are simple tapered slabs. Reads correctly at configurator distance; would want a rounded trapezoid section and machined detail to stand a close-up.

mods.$note: CarConfig has no boot-lid field, so this needs the Phase 3 schema extension before it can ship. Deliberately incompatible with nothing: ducktails and wings still mount to it because their anchors are unchanged. The badge is a separate node and is left alone.

The duct is displaced into the OEM surface rather than cut out of it, so the skin stays continuous; only the throat is a real opening. Its mouth carries a lipped surround because face deletion leaves an edge that follows the panel's topology — see blender/mods/BP03_naca_bonnet.py.

The panel IS the OEM bonnet surface, refined locally around the two apertures and solidified 4mm, so its shut lines and nose edge are correct by construction. Built by blender/mods/BP01_vented_bonnet.py.
